checks: The weighted centroid lies in the interior because the measure dominates positive volume. Brunn–Minkowski makes the projection tail root concave. The uniform volume rank is uniform, and the pushed-forward added measure has rank density bounded by L. Jensen with centroid coefficient two gives exactly (1+2α)s^(1/d)≥d/(d+1)+2∫v^(1/d)h(v)dv.

Both band lengths r/L and (α-r)/L fit their intervals by the domination inequalities. Left filling minimizes the rank integral because the signed difference has zero integral and the shifted increasing integrand has matching sign. Integrating both bands gives the stated necessary inequality. Filling the whole interval gives b, and the complement measure of mass δ gives r≥Ls-δ. The L=0 case and exact full-saturation simplex example follow directly.

Writing h=L-(L-h) loses at most δ in the rank integral. The condition makes the resulting lower bound on s^(1/d) nonnegative, so taking powers and Bernoulli is valid. Multiplying s by 1+L and subtracting δ gives E_d after substitution α=L-δ.

Independently checked the monotone ratio maxima 9/4 and 16/11 and the two exact margin coefficients. The elementary exponential series bound gives e≤87/32<11/4 and Γ_d>4/11>1/3, proving both strict positive conclusions. Tightening a containing cap preserves the lower bounds by monotonicity of both s and s+r.

Optimizes the unit-ceiling scalar feasible region for the weighted mass s+2r. Here the objective is s+r, and L may exceed one.
